heuristics.rule: Negotiate non-cash levers in priority order, not all at once
heuristics.condition: When you have multiple things you want from an offer...
heuristics.action: ...sequence asks: base salary and equity first, then signing bonus, then non-cash levers, then nice-to-haves last
heuristics.because: Negotiating everything simultaneously signals extraction-maximizing behavior; sequenced asks signal principled, specific priorities

heuristics.rule: Signing bonus is the fallback lever, not the opening ask
heuristics.condition: When salary is fixed or at the top of a band...
heuristics.action: ...exhaust salary and equity negotiation first, then pivot to signing bonus as the gap-closer
heuristics.because: Signing bonus comes from a different budget than payroll and doesn't trigger salary band violations, making it available even when base is capped

heuristics.rule: Never accept verbal agreements on remote work — insist on written confirmation in the offer letter
heuristics.condition: When a company verbally agrees to remote or hybrid arrangements...
heuristics.action: ...require the exact terms in the offer letter before signing, not just email or verbal assurance
heuristics.because: Verbal agreements are unenforceable; 'we prefer remote' in an offer letter is legally and practically different from 'this role is fully remote'

heuristics.rule: Frame PTO negotiation as matching your current package, not asking for more than standard
heuristics.action: ...anchor to what you currently have: 'I currently have 25 days — would you be able to match that?'
heuristics.because: Framing as matching avoids appearing greedy while giving the company a concrete, defensible reason to approve the exception

heuristics.rule: Push for a title upgrade if the higher level puts you in a salary band with more upside
heuristics.condition: When a title upgrade is on the table at a large tech company...
heuristics.action: ...request the higher level code because it may trigger a re-evaluation that unlocks a higher comp band
heuristics.because: Level codes at large tech companies are directly tied to salary bands; a title upgrade can be a backdoor to comp increases that HR couldn't approve directly

heuristics.rule: Negotiate relocation gross-up to cover the tax impact
heuristics.action: ...negotiate the gross amount rather than the net figure, accounting for the fact that relocation assistance is taxable income
heuristics.because: Post-2017 tax law makes relocation assistance taxable, so a $10,000 relocation package may net only $6,500–$7,000 after taxes without a gross-up

heuristics.rule: Close the negotiation with a specific, conditional commitment
heuristics.condition: When you've identified the one or two levers that matter most...
heuristics.action: ...say 'I'm excited about this role. If we can resolve [specific lever], I'm ready to sign'
heuristics.because: Clear, specific signals of good faith accelerate resolution and show you're negotiating in earnest, not endlessly maximizing

heuristics.rule: Delay your start date to avoid leaving unvested equity on the table
heuristics.condition: When you have equity vesting within weeks or months at your current employer...
heuristics.action: ...be transparent with the new employer about the vesting date and request a start date that captures that value
heuristics.because: Most companies accommodate 2–4 week delays for senior hires; the cost to them is low and the value to you can be tens of thousands of dollars

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Different levers are owned by different budget holders — hiring manager may approve remote work while HR owns salary bands, making some levers easier to move than others
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask yourself who needs to approve the specific ask; non-cash levers like pro dev budgets and remote work are often manager-level decisions, not HR committee decisions

decision_factors.factor: Whether the agreement is in writing
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Verbal commitments on remote work, PTO, or other non-cash terms are unenforceable and often forgotten or reversed after joining
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether the offer letter explicitly states the terms; if it only appears in email or verbal conversation, it is not secured

decision_factors.factor: Clawback provisions on signing bonus and relocation
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Signing bonuses and relocation packages typically require repayment if you leave within 12–24 months, which affects true value if you have any uncertainty about tenure
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Read the offer letter or separate bonus agreement for repayment clauses; confirm the repayment period and whether it prorates over time

decision_factors.factor: Title's impact on future employer evaluations
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The title you accept affects the level at which future employers evaluate and comp you; a lower title can suppress offers even if your actual scope was higher
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check what level the equivalent role is called at peer companies; ask whether the title is what would appear externally on LinkedIn

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Remote work from a lower-cost city dramatically increases effective compensation; a $200K role in NYC is equivalent to $280K+ in Austin in purchasing power
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Use cost-of-living calculators to convert nominal comp to purchasing power equivalent across candidate's actual location vs. company's location

decision_factors.factor: Start date relative to review and bonus cycle
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Starting in October vs. November can affect bonus pro-ration and when your first performance review occurs, with material comp consequences
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask HR when the company's fiscal year, review cycle, and bonus cycle begin; map your proposed start date against those milestones

decision_factors.factor: Whether PTO is guaranteed vs. accrual-based in year one
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Some companies require accrual before PTO can be used, which means you may not be able to use negotiated days until late in year one
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask explicitly: 'Is this an upfront PTO bank or does it accrue over time?' and get confirmation of first-year availability in writing

decision_factors.factor: Whether a title upgrade triggers equity re-grant at the higher level
decision_factors.why_it_matters: At some companies, a higher level code comes with equity grants calibrated to that level, making title negotiation a financial lever, not just a prestige lever
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask whether the level change comes with equity re-calibration; compare equity grant norms at the two levels using public compensation data

decision_factors.factor: Pro dev budget accessibility and rollover
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A $5,000 pro dev budget is material for active upskilling, but only if it's accessible for your specific use case and doesn't expire unused
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask what the budget covers, who approves usage, and whether unused budget rolls over or is forfeited annually

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Accepting an inflated title at a startup
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Future large-company employers will benchmark you against that inflated title level and find you don't meet the scope expectations, potentially downleveling you and suppressing comp
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Early-career professionals who use startup title inflation as a stepping stone to large tech companies

hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Signals extraction-maximizing behavior to the recruiter and hiring manager, which can sour goodwill and make them less likely to advocate for you internally
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Candidates who are negotiating their first offer and conflate thoroughness with effectiveness

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Accepting a signing bonus without reading the clawback provision
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: If you leave within 12–24 months for any reason — including being laid off or hating the role — you may owe back the full amount, creating a financial trap that delays exit
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Candidates at companies with high attrition or instability, and those who may be evaluating the role as a short-term stepping stone

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Relying on a verbal remote work agreement instead of written confirmation
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Hiring manager or team changes post-joining mean the agreement has no enforcement mechanism; you may be called back to office with no recourse
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Anyone who chose the role primarily because of remote flexibility and whose next-best alternative was a fully remote position

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Negotiating a delayed start date to capture unvested equity
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Your review cycle at the new company starts later, potentially pushing your first performance review and raise eligibility out by months
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Candidates joining companies with strict annual review cycles where start month determines review eligibility

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Taking unlimited PTO instead of negotiating a guaranteed PTO floor
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Unlimited PTO policies often result in employees taking less vacation than those with defined allocations due to social pressure and ambiguity about norms
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Candidates coming from cultures or roles where rest and personal time are already underprotected

failure_patterns.pattern: Treating non-cash levers as afterthoughts rather than primary negotiation targets
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Candidates fixate on base salary as the sole measure of offer quality, not recognizing that non-cash levers often have different, more flexible budget owners
failure_patterns.consequence: Leaving $15,000–$40,000 in total compensation value on the table that could have been captured without touching the salary band
warning_signs: Candidate accepts the offer after a single salary exchange without exploring other levers
Candidate only asks about salary and equity in their negotiation conversation

failure_patterns.pattern: Asking for everything at once in a single negotiation conversation
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Fear that there will be no second opportunity to negotiate, leading candidates to front-load all asks to avoid missing anything
failure_patterns.consequence: Appears transactional and extraction-focused; reduces recruiter and hiring manager goodwill and willingness to advocate internally
warning_signs: Candidate drafts a list of 7+ items to negotiate before any conversation begins
Candidate frames the conversation as 'here are all the things I need' rather than 'here are the one or two things that matter most'

failure_patterns.pattern: Accepting verbal commitments on remote work without written confirmation
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Candidates feel uncomfortable appearing distrustful by insisting on written terms, especially after a warm recruiter relationship has developed
failure_patterns.consequence: Remote arrangements evaporate after policy changes or manager transitions, with no contractual basis to object
warning_signs: Offer letter is silent on remote work arrangement
Recruiter says 'that's not something we typically put in writing' when asked to formalize remote terms

failure_patterns.pattern: Using signing bonus as the first negotiation ask instead of the fallback
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Candidates perceive signing bonus as the 'safe' ask because it feels less confrontational than pushing on base salary
failure_patterns.consequence: Burning the most flexible lever early, before exhausting base salary and equity, and ending up with less total comp than a sequenced approach would have yielded
warning_signs: Candidate opens with 'Can you add a signing bonus?' before any salary discussion
Candidate hasn't researched the comp band to know whether base is actually at ceiling

failure_patterns.pattern: Ignoring the tax impact of relocation packages
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Candidates focus on the gross dollar amount of the relocation offer without understanding that it is taxable income, reducing net value by 25–40%
failure_patterns.consequence: Effective relocation support is significantly lower than expected, potentially leaving the candidate underresourced during a high-cost transition
warning_signs: Candidate accepts a flat relocation number without asking about tax treatment
Candidate doesn't request a gross-up to cover the tax liability

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the remote work arrangement stated explicitly in the offer letter, or only communicated verbally?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate has actually secured flexible work terms or is operating on an informal understanding that has no enforcement mechanism
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Does it say 'fully remote' specifically, or use softer language like 'remote-friendly' or 'we prefer remote'?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Why haven't you asked for it in writing, and what is your plan if the arrangement changes after you join?

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you know which budget your target lever (remote, PTO, pro dev, signing bonus) comes from — salary/HR or the hiring manager's discretionary budget?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate understands who actually has the authority to approve the ask, which determines how to route the request
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you framed your ask to the right decision-maker, or are you going through HR for something the hiring manager could approve directly?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: You may be negotiating with the wrong person; ask the recruiter who owns approval for each specific lever before making the ask

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the signing bonus have a clawback provision, and if so, what is the repayment window and does it prorate?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: The true financial risk of the signing bonus relative to how long you expect to stay and how certain you are about the role
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Is the clawback full repayment or prorated? How does that affect your break-even tenure?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: You need to read the offer letter or bonus agreement carefully before signing — this is almost always present and is a material financial obligation

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the title you're being offered match the scope of work you'll actually be doing, and does it match equivalent roles at peer companies?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate is being underleveled, which affects both immediate equity grants and long-term career trajectory at future employers
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you confirmed whether the title is what would appear externally, and whether a title upgrade would trigger a comp band re-evaluation?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Push for a title that reflects the scope; use the framing 'the work you've described sounds like a [higher level] — can the title reflect that?'

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you mapped your proposed start date against the company's review cycle and bonus pro-ration schedule?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate is inadvertently starting at a time that defers their first performance review and bonus eligibility by months
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Is there a start date within 2–4 weeks of your current target that would put you inside the current review cycle rather than the next one?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Ask HR explicitly: when does the fiscal year begin, when are reviews, and how is bonus pro-rated for someone starting at my proposed date?

diagnostic_questions.question: Are you negotiating 2–3 specific levers with clear rationale, or presenting a broad list of everything you'd like?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate's negotiation posture signals principled asks or extraction-maximizing behavior, which affects recruiter and hiring manager goodwill
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Good — make sure each ask has a concrete framing (matching current package, role scope alignment, one-time vs. recurring cost) rather than just 'I'd like more'
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Prioritize ruthlessly to 2–3 levers; decide which matter most and which are true nice-to-haves you're willing to drop to close

industry_realities.common_belief: If the salary is fixed or at the top of the band, there's nothing left to negotiate
industry_realities.actual_reality: Non-cash levers like signing bonus, PTO, remote work, pro dev budget, and title are often owned by different budget holders than base salary and remain fully negotiable even when base is at ceiling
industry_realities.implication: Candidates should treat a salary ceiling as the trigger to pivot to non-cash levers, not as the end of negotiation

industry_realities.common_belief: PTO negotiation costs the company real money, so they're unlikely to flex on it
industry_realities.actual_reality: PTO doesn't cost the company direct cash — it costs coverage capacity — and adjustments typically don't require HR committee approval or trigger salary band reviews
industry_realities.implication: PTO is often one of the easiest levers to move because the approval path is short and the cash cost is indirect; it should be a standard ask

industry_realities.common_belief: A verbal commitment from a hiring manager or recruiter on remote work is reliable
industry_realities.actual_reality: Verbal agreements on remote work have no enforcement mechanism; manager changes, policy shifts, or return-to-office mandates can nullify them with no recourse for the employee
industry_realities.implication: Remote work terms must appear explicitly in the offer letter with precise language; anything short of that is not a secured benefit

industry_realities.common_belief: An inflated title at a startup is a career asset because it looks impressive
industry_realities.actual_reality: Large tech employers benchmark candidates against the scope expectations of that title level; an inflated title that doesn't match your actual scope can cause downleveling and comp suppression at the next role
industry_realities.implication: Evaluate title upgrades at startups against how they will be interpreted by your next employer, not just how they sound

industry_realities.common_belief: Negotiating multiple things at once is more efficient and shows you know what you want
industry_realities.actual_reality: Presenting a long list of asks signals extraction-maximizing behavior and reduces recruiter and hiring manager willingness to advocate internally on your behalf
industry_realities.implication: Prioritize to 2–3 levers with specific rationale; sequential, targeted asks produce better outcomes than comprehensive lists

industry_realities.common_belief: Relocation packages are straightforward dollar amounts you can spend on moving expenses
industry_realities.actual_reality: Post-2017 tax law makes relocation assistance taxable income, so a $10,000 relocation package may net only $6,000–$7,500 without a gross-up negotiation
industry_realities.implication: Always negotiate the gross amount of the relocation package and explicitly request a gross-up to cover the tax liability, not just the nominal dollar figure

industry_realities.common_belief: Remote work is a lifestyle perk with no financial value
industry_realities.actual_reality: Remote work eliminates $2,000–$8,000/year in commuting costs and can provide a purchasing power equivalent of tens of thousands of dollars annually when working from a lower-cost city
industry_realities.implication: Remote work flexibility should be evaluated and negotiated as a financial benefit, not just a convenience preference

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Treats negotiation as a single salary conversation; once base salary is agreed, considers the negotiation closed
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Treats negotiation as a multi-lever process across base, equity, signing bonus, non-cash benefits, title, and start date — each addressed in sequence
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Senior practitioners capture $15,000–$40,000 in additional value that juniors leave on the table by not knowing to ask

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Accepts the framing that a fixed salary means there is nothing left to negotiate
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Recognizes that a salary ceiling is the trigger to pivot to signing bonus and non-cash levers, which often have separate budget owners and more flexibility
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: The ability to unlock value when the primary lever is constrained is the core skill that separates effective negotiators from ineffective ones

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Accepts a verbal or informal assurance from the recruiter and considers the remote arrangement secured
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Insists on explicit written terms in the offer letter with precise language before considering any remote arrangement binding
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Verbal agreements provide no protection when policies change or managers turn over; seniors understand enforcement mechanisms, not just goodwill

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Evaluates title based on how it sounds or looks on a resume in isolation
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Evaluates title based on how it maps to comp bands, equity grant levels, and how future employers will interpret and benchmark it
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Title decisions have compounding financial effects across multiple future jobs; treating title as purely symbolic misses significant long-term comp impact

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Lists every possible ask at once to avoid missing anything, treating thoroughness as a virtue
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Prioritizes to 2–3 levers with specific rationale, making clean asks sequentially to preserve goodwill and negotiating capital
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Recruiter and hiring manager goodwill is a resource that gets depleted; spending it on low-priority asks reduces their willingness to advocate for high-priority ones

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Uses signing bonus as an early or opening ask because it feels like a 'safe' request that won't offend
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Reserves signing bonus as the fallback lever after exhausting base salary and equity, because it's the most flexible budget and should close remaining gaps
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Sequencing preserves the signing bonus as a gap-closer rather than burning it early before understanding what gaps actually need closing

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Asks for more PTO as a general preference without anchoring to a specific number or rationale
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Anchors PTO ask to current package: 'I have 25 days now — can you match that?' and requests written confirmation of the guaranteed amount
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Anchored asks with clear rationale are easier for managers to approve internally; vague requests have no internal advocacy story
